title: Surgical Strike
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.2 — Surgical Strike (7-Ply Mission)
description: Mission 1 walkthrough: when your Hub can be captured next turn it is hanging — refuse that, then convert a Beam file into Surgical Strike. From the Fleet Academy advanced manual.

scenes.headline: Surgical Strike
scenes.subhead: Grow the net, keep the Hub safe, end the game.
scenes.voiceover: Episode two: Surgical Strike. A short highlight reel. One rule to learn before the board moves: if the opponent can capture your Command Hub on their next turn, your Hub is hanging. Refuse the hang means fix that before you chase your own attack.

scenes.headline: What “refuse the hang” means
bullets: Hanging = they can capture your Hub next turn
The engine allows it — you lose if they take it
Refuse the hang = keep the Hub safe first
scenes.voiceover: A ship is hanging when the opponent can take it on their next turn. In Subspace Lattice the only hang that ends the mission is the Command Hub. The rules do not stop you from leaving it exposed — that is legal — but if they capture it, you lose immediately by Surgical Strike. So refuse the hang means: never leave your Hub capturable next turn, and if it already is, capture or block the threat before you fire your own prepared shot.
Starting position. White already holds the Initiative Relay Escort forward. Black’s Hub sits on a file White’s Beam can eventually claim — if the net opens and the Hub stays safe.
Ply one. White pushes the relay Escort. Deepening the foothold grows midboard coverage so later Beam fire has somewhere to live.
Ply two. Black does not yet contest the Beam’s file — a quiet side step while White telegraphs net-building on the left.
Ply three. White slides an Escort beside the Beam’s file — extending the blue glow toward Black’s Hub without sitting on the lane and blocking the shot.

scenes.prompt: Black just stepped next to White’s Hub. Is White’s Hub hanging?
scenes.voiceover: Ply four. Black steps next to White’s Hub. That Hub is now hanging — Black can capture it next turn and win. Pause and predict: if White ignores this and stares at the Beam shot, Black takes Surgical Strike.
scenes.revealVoiceover: Ply five. White refuses the hang: the Hub was one capture from dying, so White captures the threatening Escort instead of firing the Beam. The prepared shot can wait one ply. Hub safety always comes first.

scenes.voiceover: Ply six. Black’s trap failed. Tempo lost — and Black’s Hub is still sitting on White’s Beam file.
Ply seven. Net open, Hub safe, enemy Hub on the Beam’s file. White converts preparation into Surgical Strike — the usual way fleet games end when the plan works.

scenes.headline: Lesson: if the Hub can die next, fix that first
scenes.voiceover: Core lesson: a hanging Hub is a Hub the opponent can capture next turn. Refuse that before material, nets, or your own Strike. Next: a chess-length battle — openings, trade fights, and a walk-in finish.
